mn107:2.2: The Commentary does not gloss this simile, but the reference is evidently to the building work by which such a stairway is progressively completed. Cf. Sutta 85, where it is likewise clear that ‘last’ (pacchima) refers to the bottom step.
mn107:3.4: The Pātimokkha is the name for the code of 227 rules that are fundamental to the bhikkhu’s life. They are recited on full-moon and new-moon days in the presence of all the bhikkhus resident in a monastery.
mn107:5.4: Cf. the simile of moderation in eating at Saṃyutta XXII, 84.
mn107:6.2: ‘Overlapping’ (accādhāya) is not found in the P.T.S. Dictionary; see also Sutta 39.
mn107:15.2: The translator notes ‘(distracted)’ as an alternative sense for ‘haughty’ (uddhata) here.
